general_information.Description: This course introduces students to the principles and trade-offs in designing data-intensive systems, using Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd Edition) as the primary textbook. Students will study: 1. Trade-offs in data systems architecture: OLTP vs OLAP, Cloud vs Self-Hosting, Distributed vs Single-Node systems. 2. Nonfunctional requirements: Scalability, Reliability, and Maintainability. 3. Data models: Relational, Document, and Graph-Like models. 4. Storage and retrieval: LSM-tree, B-Trees, columnar storage, Cloud Data Warehouses. 5. Batch processing: MapReduce and Apache Spark on large-scale public datasets. 6. Stream processing: Change Data Capture (CDC), Kafka/Redpanda, log-based messaging. 7. Data encoding: JSON, Protocol Buffers, Avro, schema evolution. 8. Distributed systems: Replication, Sharding, Transactions, and Isolation. 9. End-to-end data pipeline design from OLTP ingestion to OLAP analytical output.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - Docker Desktop (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) - Python 3.10+ (https://www.python.org/) - VS Code (https://code.visualstudio.com/) - Git (https://git-scm.com/) - DBeaver (https://dbeaver.io/) — for PostgreSQL, ClickHouse - Internet Tools provided via Docker: - PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB - Apache Spark (bitnami/spark) - Redpanda (Kafka-compatible) - MinIO (S3-compatible object storage) - ClickHouse (OLAP analytics) Minimum hardware requirement: - RAM ≥ 8GB (16GB recommended for Lab 05 full-stack CDC pipeline) - Free disk space ≥ 20GB - CPU: 4 cores or more recommended

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze trade-offs and nonfunctional requirements of data systems, including OLTP versus OLAP, scalability, reliability, and maintainability.
Compare data models, storage engines, and encoding formats to select appropriate solutions for given workloads.
Explain replication, sharding, and transaction isolation in distributed data systems.
Apply batch processing techniques to analyze large datasets using Apache Spark and Spark SQL.
Build streaming data pipelines and design end-to-end systems from OLTP to OLAP.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Why do you think modern companies choose to separate their transaction processing systems (OLTP) from their analytics systems (OLAP), even though this adds complexity?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: How would you explain to a non-technical manager why a system that works perfectly with 100 users might fail with 1 million users — and what would you do about it?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Why might choosing a document database over a relational database for a social network make the application faster to build but harder to maintain over time?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4
